ateret-zekenim/5:_: There are those who permit entirely. But when he rents an oven to a non-Jew on condition he bake matzot in it and the non-Jew baked chametz and matzah in it, it is permitted according to all — the Jew will think he receives his wage for baking matzah in it, not for the chametz.
ateret-zekenim/7:_: Forbidden to rent a utensil to a non-Jew on Pesach so he cook chametz in it, for he profits from issurei hana'ah; but permitted to rent a utensil before Pesach with Pesach days absorbed, such as renting for three or four weeks to do in it what he wishes, even though it is known the non-Jew will cook chametz in it during Pesach — for he will consider all his wage for days before Pesach and after Pesach, and there is no profiting from issurei hana'ah. One stringent even in this — see there (Maharam MiRotenburg). Those holding an estate and taking from them measures of maltz from every beer wage cooked in cauldrons — the law changes by the estate arrangement: if the cauldrons belong to the lord who rents and the Jew must repair cauldrons when broken, and even if cauldrons age the Jew must buy new ones himself and deliver complete at estate payment time — then cauldrons are in the Jew's possession; needless to say forbidden to take the measures themselves, for the Jew acquired them as cauldron-wage and it is actual chametz over which Passover passed; but even money forbidden, like benefiting from actual chametz money, since their custom is to give chametz itself as cauldron-wage, as explained in responsum of R' Shimon. Even when he takes nothing it would appear forbidden because of wanting its continued existence; but since he cannot prevent cooking because they pay his wage per the estate, he is compelled — if he can prevent their cooking, forbidden l'chatchila to let them cook because of wanting its continued existence; and it was explained permission is through sale — sell before Pesach to a non-Jew all measures coming from the week of Pesach and take money immediately; even though the non-Jew sells and returns measures after Pesach, permitted. But if an estate where the Jew need not repair cauldrons at all — they cook in their own, only took measures from every cooking — then similar to buying the priests' allotment: stipulate with the non-Jew before Pesach to give money; b'dieved may receive measures even without stipulation; if he does not know who cooked, stipulate with him — like b'dieved (my teacher in Bach).
beur-hagra/2:_: Seif 2 — A Jew who receives etc. For he did not acquire them; and even without statement, by law permitted as Tosafot Avodah Zarah 22a s.v. lo yomar wrote. However, where etc. — specifically stated; and all the more here; and see seif 3.
beur-hagra/3:_: Seif 3 — A Jew and a non-Jew. As written regarding orlah for Rashi's explanation; and further siman 494 seif 13 in the gloss.
beur-hagra/4:א: Seif 4 — A Jew etc. for it is etc. On seif 2 (1) — his wage etc. and we learned "he sold them" etc.; and see there Tosafot s.v. vehatnan. However, it is wondrous etc.
beur-hagra/4:ב: And if he received etc. — permitted. It implies even he himself, as Rambam wrote siman 443 and as the Gemara's plain meaning in Avodah Zarah there; and see Tosafot there s.v. tenan. It is wondrous etc.; but here it is reconciled; and see Ran perek 5 of Avodah Zarah who brought proof from Yerushalmi and wrote in the Yerushalmi, in the name of Ramban: what we conclude there is a fine they fined carriers and innkeepers specifically for innkeepers in shevi'it when produce takes its value and forbidden by first reasoning that produce takes its value — relies etc. (end of his words). Seif 5 — there: he rented to dwell etc.; and see Gemara there 65a — "if so" etc.; and likewise here, he takes nothing for the chametz, for even if he does not bake at all he will pay him.
beur-hagra/4:ג: And likewise permitted. We learn from the above; but to rent that he bring chametz inside is forbidden as Yerushalmi chapter 2 halacha 2: a Jew shall not rent his house to a non-Jew to place chametz inside; and even though they said in first chapter of Pesachim he designated a house etc. — here it deals during Pesach or erev Pesach when already forbidden in benefit — profiting from issurei hana'ah as above; and so Yerushalmi there during Pesach deals during Pesach — what if etc. and it was taught do not rent etc.; and Taz and Magen Avraham; and see Bach in the name of Agur. It appears to me that also that in Pesachim first chapter deals during Pesach, as there the baraita teaches a non-Jew entered etc. — therefore during Pesach; and above it says he deposited etc., designated etc. — to say etc.; rather there it deals when he designated a house not to bring chametz in, and permitted even when he brings inside as above; and on this they said there a non-Jew when it says etc. — to say etc.; and it was taught etc. — there too renting a dwelling, and nevertheless forbidden; and Geonim explain unlike Rashi — rather he designated a house: he rents him another house not in his house; and this is "a non-Jew entered etc." — since he is with the chametz deposited etc., even without liability he designated etc. without liability, since it is another house; and so in Yerushalmi there: a non-Jew's chametz during Pesach — what? R' Yirmiyah said permitted, R' Yissa forbidden; and it was taught: do not rent one's donkey to a non-Jew to bring chametz on it — explain it when it comes with him; and it was taught do not rent his house etc. — you may say when it comes with him; therefore even for one who permits, forbidden with him in the house; and this is what is written in Tosafot; and above siman 448 seif 3 outside the house.
beur-hagra/6:א: Seif 6 — Permitted etc. Avodah Zarah 63 — a person tells his workers etc.
beur-hagra/6:ב: And some permit. There — R' Papa etc., R' Ashi etc.; and the first version too, only he relied on what is written in Yoreh De'ah.
beur-hagra/6:ג: And forbidden. Lest he come to eat, as first chapter Pesachim 10:11; and Yerushalmi above for one who permits establishes it when it comes with him as above; and even Rabanan explain only because he himself etc.; and above siman 346 seif 3 — this is pushing with a reed specifically. Further there is no agency for a non-Jew, as Bava Metzia 71b; and even though the Jew does not intend to buy, nevertheless he is liable for it and transgresses; and further he wants its continued existence as Avodah Zarah 64a — behold he wants etc.
beur-hagra/7:ב: But one may rent. Tosefta chapter 2; but in Yerushalmi it was taught forbidden whether in house, ship, or donkey; and so Geonim; and as written regarding innkeeper there 62a; and no difference between yayin nesech and other prohibitions except b'dieved to seize its value as above; and even if it did not come with him forbidden as Yerushalmi there and Yoreh De'ah siman 332 seif 1 (end of his words); and so in gloss above seif 5.
beur-hagra/7:ג: And some permit. Meaning he disagrees with Tur and Shulchan Aruch who wrote forbidden to rent etc. even though for donkey permitted as Tur wrote because of wanting continued existence through something else as Avodah Zarah 32a — we hold like those who forbid there; but Tosafot there s.v. vehai permit in such a case as written there etc.; and we rule like those who permit etc.; and he does not disagree where they forbade renting, for even for one's donkey forbidden as above; therefore wrote and some permit heating etc.
biur-halacha/2:_: He should tell him before Pesach — see Taz who divided here: stipulation before Pesach does not help except when he did not lend for a fixed time but each week holding his money pays him interest — with this stipulation before Pesach helps, like a gift at loan start, for if he wanted he could remove his money; but if he lent for a term and within the term neither can withdraw and he is obligated to give loaves each week — stipulation before Pesach does not help, only stipulate at loan start, like siman 245 regarding Jew-non-Jew partnership for Shabbat. However, from Magen Avraham s.k. 2 it implies no division here; see Machatzit HaShekel and Peri Megadim; and so Noda BiYehudah and Chamed Moshe rejected Taz's words (see there). It appears their words are not compelled except when reconciling both that on Pesach he gives money; but when the Jew stipulates alone and the non-Jew does not agree to change prior terms, there may well be room for Taz — the Jew cannot change initial terms. See Peri Megadim who also hesitated on Taz and wrote the first condition is not strong since there was no pulling and it is something not yet come (see there); concludes nevertheless where dina demalkhuta is that conditions stand, be stringent like Taz; b'dieved requires further study (see there). In my humble opinion even there no stringency b'dieved: though dina demalkhuta obligates giving loaves, he has only a debt of loaves, not that the loaves themselves belong to the Jew even before entering his possession, as we wrote in Mishna Berurah; and so we found in Beit Meir (end of his words).
biur-halacha/7:א: Forbidden to rent a utensil — see Mishna Berurah: Tur's reason because of wanting its continued existence; and there are opinions among Acharonim whether specifically in rental or even borrowing has prohibition of wanting continued existence; see Kaf HaChayyim and Ma'agalei Tzedek.
biur-halacha/7:ב: On Pesach — and proven from Shulchan Aruch of the Gra that for wanting continued existence there is no permission — Agur when renting before Pesach in all cases forbidden. However Bach implies whether profiting or wanting continued existence, in all cases there is room to permit however it was before thirty [days] (and he wrote so per his version in Agur, and likewise those who read before Pesach); and so Ma'agalei Tzedek wrote; and know further: even for those who hold prohibition of wanting continued existence applies to chametz — only l'chatchila; b'dieved no stringency, as above seif 4 regarding profiting from issurei hana'ah; and so Peri Chadash wrote; and see Chamed Moshe what he wrote on this.
chatam-sofer/1:_: On Mechaber seif 2 — A Jew who receives. Note: regarding estate-holders who give wage and deposit to innkeepers to sell — see responsa Chatam Sofer Orach Chayim siman 118 [regarding an estate-holder Jew selling barrels of deposit to a non-Jew and Wirtshauser — their custom and liability etc., and he wrote in his view transgresses because chametz need not be literally yours — since available and he has a grasp it is called his, etc.; nullification does not help since not his to declare ownerless, only a mere grasp; but before Pesach must buy from Wirtshauser to cancel first acquisition and draw again as complete purchase].
chatam-sofer/2:_: (There Magen Avraham s.k. 11) s.v. shelo yibaka — note: see tractate Avodah Zarah 68b — so sparks not fly etc. (end of his words); and there Magen Avraham's explanation does not apply (end of his words); requires further study.
chatam-sofer/3:_: (There s.k. 12) The reason — see siman 442 seif 2; the second was erased; note: wondrous in Magen Avraham s.k. 6 (end of his words); requires further study.
chok-yaakov/1:_: He must repay after Pesach. Tur wrote there is no prohibition of chametz over which Passover passed — he learned from what is in the beginning of the chapter of the hirer in Beit Rabbi Yannai: the poor borrow produce from the poor in shevi'it and repay in the eighth; Tosafot wrote there: since at that hour those fruits are not in existence they are not substitutes; therefore if they repaid in shevi'it itself, also permitted by this reason — since fruits are not in existence they are not called shevi'it substitutes (end of his words); all the more here with chametz that does not take its value — it was at permitted time, permitted to receive money even during Pesach; therefore somewhat difficult why they wrote he must repay after Pesach — likewise even during Pesach permitted; and what the Gemara stated there "and they repaid in the eighth" — they cited an incident that occurred. Truly at the start of the Rosh's words there it implies the main permission reason is since shevi'it year passed; but from the end of his words it is clear he agrees with Tosafot — since not in existence, not called shevi'it substitutes; the difficulty returns; possibly therefore poskim stated after Pesach to show even if he again pays loaves it is permitted in such a case. And Kenesset HaGedolah wrote there are places that practiced forbidding l'chatchila to borrow before Pesach and repay after Pesach because of interest concern — forbidden to lend se'ah bese'ah; see Yoreh De'ah siman 462 seif 1 in gloss explaining loaves for loaves permitted to lend.
chok-yaakov/2:א: Flour. See above siman 453 seif 4 — which flour is not held for chametz.
chok-yaakov/2:ב: And since he stipulated thus with him. Here, even though there are some differences of opinion in this law, the main thing appears as Shulchan Aruch and Levush imply — l'chatchila good to stipulate thus (and see Rokeach siman 268); and if he stipulates thus, even if the non-Jew later gives chametz over which Passover passed, also permitted; and if he did not stipulate, if the non-Jew gives afterwards flour or money or chametz made after Pesach, permitted — chametz substitutes permitted like chametz of transgressors, as explained above siman 443; and same law for one who buys the non-Jew's allotment who give fixed bread every week — see Tur and Beit Yosef; and do not be stringent in these laws, for without this a Jew does not acquire without pulling per most poskim — see Choshen Mishpat 194 and Shach there s.k. 1.
chok-yaakov/3:_: And I will take afterwards. Then permitted to take even chametz — so Beit Yosef from Mordechai first chapter of Avodah Zarah; and so Agudah; and see in Acharonim' words what they divide between this law and depleting siman 245 — Jew and non-Jew with field partnership forbidden to tell him take yours for Shabbat and mine for weekday. Bach wrote one should be stringent here too unless he takes money for his share before Pesach — so Acharonim for practical law. Nevertheless on Shabbat within Pesach what he said "take yours" does not help as other Shabbats of the year, as above siman 245, unless they stipulated at partnership start (end of his words); and Magen Avraham wrote: and on four days that are yom tov in any event forbidden to tell him take yours as in siman 245 (end of his words). I wondered at the view — how did no posek omit to write this law here, all wrote blanket permission on Pesach implying even yom tov itself permitted; and do not say entirely to siman 245, for the main prohibition reason there as Gemara and poskim — as if the non-Jew does melacha forbidden as the Jew's agent. That is specifically field melacha or renting oven on Shabbat — not so yom tov where burning for need is permitted for the Jew himself — all the more no prohibition concern if the non-Jew acts as his agent; here only chametz-substitute concern poskim mentioned — saying "take yours" suffices.
chok-yaakov/4:א: Even money forbidden to receive. Since the oven belongs to the Jew; and do not say for seif 3 that there it is partnership oven; and see Taz s.k. 3 who wrote there are divided opinions in these two seifim and wonders on Shulchan Aruch; and see Kenesset HaGedolah who lengthily proved no dispute at all — and that is the main point.
chok-yaakov/4:ב: For it is profiting from issurei hana'ah. See this siman — Bach on what is practiced in Russia and Volhynia: Jews rent an estate with cauldrons and mills taking a measure from every beer wage and from everyone grinding maltz — if the Jew must repair cauldrons and mills when broken, they are in the Jew's possession, forbidden even money as wage, since their custom is to give chametz — like benefiting from chametz money, forbidden; if he can prevent them from cooking he must, wanting continued existence; permission through sale — sell before Pesach to a non-Jew all measures from this week, take money, even if non-Jew returns measures afterwards, permitted; if Jew need not repair, suffice to stipulate before Pesach as seif 2; if no one to stipulate with, b'dieved permitted without condition (end). Taz is stringent even if Jew need not repair; Magen Avraham in this siman sides to be lenient — since mills belong to whole city and estate-holder cannot protest non-Jew grinding that day — properly can say he is not pleased to acquire at prohibition time; I did not want to extend further in this law since their estate custom was hidden from me.
chok-yaakov/5:א: On condition he bake matzah in it. Rashba learned this law from what is in the Gemara beginning chapter of the hirer: hired for another work with him, even though he told him pass wine barrels — permitted; at first glance no proof from that sugya for one who examines there; and even though Beit Yosef wrote Rashba explains that mishnah another method — his words are very strained; as Netziv also expanded — see there; Rashba's proof must be: just as there, even though he passed yayin nesech barrels, since he did not hire for that, hiring permitted; if so here too, even if he did not bake chametz he would have to give wage because he did not hire for chametz; and even if he baked nothing he would owe oven-rent for that hiring — permitted; so appears Magen Avraham's implication — see there.
chok-yaakov/5:ב: And if he bakes chametz in it. Taz challenged this law and wrote: it is very difficult, for it is written siman 256 seif 3 — but it does not help if he stipulates with the non-Jew that his animal rest on Shabbat, for the non-Jew is not trusted; all the more here he will certainly bake chametz; requires further study (end). I did not grasp his intent at all — no difficulty here, unrelated: there a person is commanded regarding his animal's rest, therefore non-Jew not trusted, forbidden to rent; not so here — is a person commanded that a non-Jew not bake chametz in his oven? Only forbidden to benefit from chametz wage; if so, whoever does not rent to a non-Jew to bake chametz, not taking chametz wage — even if non-Jew certainly bakes chametz, he does not benefit from chametz wage and his wage is permitted — requires further study.
chok-yaakov/5:ג: A house to dwell. Agreement of Rishonim and Acharonim: even though he rented unstipulated to dwell, it comes only to exclude renting explicitly for chametz when renting during Pesach or erev Pesach; see Magen Avraham s.k. 11 accordingly. What is in our Gemara first chapter Pesachim 7b — he designated a house, not concerned to burn — deals renting a house as sugya implies for dwelling, and nevertheless permitted to rent; must say there it deals renting unstipulated or some time before Pesach; if so no contradiction to Yerushalmi forbidding renting; unlike Rashba responsum 177 brought in Beit Yosef siman 440 — Yerushalmi disputes our Talmud implying our Talmud permits renting in every case unless he takes wage to sit and guard — see his lengthy words. Truly we need not divide from equals — no dispute; as Agur and unstipulated Rama etc. In responsum Sha'arei Ephraim siman 16 he wrote: if a Jew sits and guards whether to forbid because of wanting prohibition's continued existence; concludes: it appears permitted; and his son in gloss wrote the reason: since he sits and does no prohibition by hand, not like wanting continued existence. For some reason distinguish when hired to do yayin nesech with him — see there; his words are wondrous, for explicitly Yoreh De'ah siman 332 seif 16 — even to guard free, forbidden wanting prohibition's continued existence; if so obviously also for chametz. Also hidden from him Rashba's responsum I wrote who is lenient on rental but stringent not to sit and guard — clear; and on Sha'arei Ephraim responsum itself A.L. wrote: meaning permitted — hiring permitted; do not say yayin nesech hiring forbidden as Rashba responsum brought Beit Yosef siman 440 — requires further study.
chok-yaakov/6:א: But he should not tell him go and eat. If known he will eat chametz — so Magen Avraham; and so poskim' implication Yoreh De'ah siman 332; and so Agudah chapter of the hirer; and somewhat against Gemara language implying forbidden even for mere concern.
chok-yaakov/6:ב: And some permit. Since he brought first opinion unstipulated, implies he tends to be stringent like first opinion as his way in Shulchan Aruch; and so Bach and Kenesset HaGedolah, even though in Biur seif 332 for yayin nesech he ruled lenient; Tur ruled lenient there without giving dinar beforehand or designating dinar; here ruled unstipulated stringent — must say chametz stringency is different; and so in Perishah gloss there; and from Bach's words who ruled lenient like Rashba, here stringent; I expanded all this to exclude Magen Avraham's view who wrote last opinion is main, requiring specifically dinar beforehand and dinar still in shopkeeper's hand as Yoreh De'ah siman 332 — that is not so; Acharonim agreed different here because of chametz stringency. Therefore one with child or sick in house needing to eat or drink chametz should command a non-Jew to give chametz, not say "and I will pay"; or carry child outside house; in any event not touch chametz — all when possible and he has a non-Jew who will do so; if not and great need for child or sick, do whatever possible — where danger everything permitted (above siman 326 and responsum Nachalat Shiva siman 14). Nevertheless good to make ten-[tefach] partition so he not eat from it; see Magen Avraham siman 443 and what Mishna Berurah wrote this siman s.k. 9.
chok-yaakov/7:א: But one may rent a donkey to bring chametz and his wage permitted. Bach and Kenesset HaGedolah dispute this — what is written regarding oven and house rent for chametz forbidden as above; see responsum of Geonim siman 243 forbidding renting (and see Bach what he wrote to reconcile Tur's words — Magen Avraham disputes, his words not compelled, only reconciling Tur). See Magen Avraham who answered: here deals with unstipulated donkey-rent not specifying to bring chametz; truly against poskim' plain language and Tosafot explicitly teaching to bring chametz — implies even when specified permitted; must be Beit Yosef and rabbi hold: since donkey permission found explicitly in Tosafot to permit, do not be stringent for chametz that does not take its value; but do not learn elsewhere — say specifically for donkey the non-Jew brings into his possession and acquires through rental, therefore permitted to rent, unlike oven and house called the Jew's name — stringent; and for utensils forbidden to rent lest he cook inside — wanting prohibition's continued existence lest vessel crack; if so even free lending forbidden, as Acharonim explained; see Levush. Nevertheless also to rent donkey explicitly for chametz — be stringent per Acharonim; see wanting continued existence in books Mishna Berurah chapter 80 s.k. 14 and Taz and Yoreh De'ah siman 332; see Magen Avraham who wrote also forbidding buying chametz on Pesach is from wanting continued existence; Rivash wrote other reasons: no agency for non-Jew, Jew ends up buying; concern lest eat from it; see responsum Sha'arei Ephraim siman 16 gloss — even if not touching chametz, concern lest eat; and as written above siman 449.
chok-yaakov/7:ב: To bring chametz on it. Law of unloading and loading regarding chametz — see Choshen Mishpat siman 272 regarding yayin nesech; see Magen Avraham s.k. 10.
chok-yaakov/7:ג: And likewise other benefit needs. Such as to place cold temporarily on dry or moist non-food item such as bathing — specifically temporary so we are not concerned for other use (above siman 451). So I brought in Mishna Berurah chapter 80 s.k. 14 and Taz; I sat there on the rabbi's words as correct, unlike Netziv; and so appears Acharonim' agreement here; see responsum Radbaz siman 504; and Acharonim on estate matter above s.k. 16 what is written there.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 3 — A Jew and a non-Jew with partnership oven etc. Note: see Magen Avraham s.k. 3 who wrote on four yom tov days forbidden to tell him take yours etc.; see Kaf HaChayyim what he challenged; see Chiddushei Orach Chayim in Choshen Mishpat siman 330 what he wrote. Further his words are wondrous from explicit baraita Avodah Zarah 21 — explicit in baraita one may not rent a bathhouse to a non-Jew where the non-Jew does melacha on Shabbats and yom tov — therefore yom tov too is stated; on yom tov burning is permitted for the Jew — if we say this burning not for equal need of all souls is forbidden to him, therefore we are concerned for the non-Jew — if so here too when the non-Jew bakes for himself, all the more if he bakes chametz — if the Jew did so for the non-Jew, especially chametz, it would be doing a Torah prohibition "for you and not for non-Jews" — therefore concern even for non-Jew. Possibly Kaf HaChayyim's intent: since truly renting oven to non-Jew or saying take yours etc., he is not his agent and no prohibition only because of melacha as siman 443 and 244 — on Shabbat forbidden; in bathhouse it is recognizable and marit ayin; here not recognizable if non-Jew bakes for himself or Jew — no marit ayin, onlooker says for Jew's need permitted for Jew, especially since anyway can be attributed to Jew; two leniencies — like field permitted; see Taz siman 244 and understand. However possibly one may say even Magen Avraham was stringent only on Pesach where erev Pesach mostly chametz vs matzah recognizable by crack or blushing faces; also Jews do not bake through non-Jews on Pesach, they guard their dough — then like bathhouse where Gemara Avodah Zarah says bathhouse for guests people do not do — likewise on Pesach not through non-Jews, therefore known he bakes for non-Jew's need and marit ayin concern; but other yom tov possibly Kaf HaChayyim is right that on yom tov permitted to say take yours — no marit ayin they will say for Jew's need — two leniencies like field; to reduce dispute, better to decide for practical law; see Chiddussei Avodah Zarah what is written; see my composition on Orach Chayim mishnah 592 daf 68 what reconciles his words (end of his words); examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (There seif 6 in gloss) And forbidden to buy chametz for a non-Jew on Pesach etc. Note: see Magen Avraham what he wrote in the name of Rivash if the Jew bought chametz for the non-Jew etc.; and see responsum to community Scali in my composition Yoreh De'ah siman 45 where I expanded at length to reconcile Rivash and Magen Avraham from what one challenged from Rashi Bava Metzia first chapter regarding raising a found object for one's fellow and Tosafot Bava Kama 102b s.v. umida yedia etc. (end of his words); examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (There seif 7) Forbidden to rent utensil to non-Jew on Pesach to cook chametz etc. Note: regarding selling grain and all utensils related — if permitted for non-Jew to make beer or rent on Pesach — simple permission in my humble opinion: needless to say if selling maltz already full chametz, obviously permitted, entire sale only d'rabbanan, bittul alone suffices; if so what difference sale thus or non-Jew does what he wishes; especially custom to sell beer and brew in Jew's house — no greater publicity and marit ayin; what prohibition in making beer or rent more than mixing. Even if selling grain and he makes maltz on Pesach [and I was told beer only from maltz made quarter-year prior] — also no prohibition, for we do not say since not chametz before and not in nullification scope, sale again ineffective evasion and Torah-level; also not novel — many Acharonim lenient even selling animals to feed chametz, challenged on grain; if so evasion helps even Torah-level, such is custom, impossible to uphold religion forbidding this. Not worse than animal sale which is certainly Torah prohibition. Further truth: Chak Yosef siman 434 wrote what became chametz on Pesach not in nullification scope — error, since such nullification does not help — require three before, nullification in heart does not help; main reason as Ran: since anyway not in his possession, mere revelation he is not pleased suffices; such revelation helps even before it becomes chametz, since when it rises it will not be in his possession — made as if in his possession; if he revealed beforehand he is not pleased in chametz, since initial revelation, Scripture did not later place in his possession. Proof from Pesachim 7 — student before rabbi remembered rolled dough in house, feared lest it become chametz — preceded and nullified before it became chametz etc.; how did baraita there say nullify in heart — nullification in heart does not help while still permitted, and perforce helps even after time; proves nullification helps even chametz that fermented during Pesach since he revealed initially. Do not say there he intended this but for chametz he did not intend to leaven — nullification does not help; possibly Chak Yosef's intent; but truly we come from revelation logic — what difference this or that, Scripture did not place in his possession as he revealed not pleased — likewise here since he revealed not pleased in chametz, automatically Scripture did not treat as in his possession, automatically not his. Further he says seen and not seen, hidden and not hidden — all included. Even if poskim's intent only if some chametz became chametz on Pesach he did not know at nullification time — but here he knew initially it will become chametz on Pesach — exact law of rolled dough explicitly nullification helps; sale again only d'rabbanan; on contrary sale on Pesach helps even to do melacha on Shabbat; and do not say yom tov where Chak Yaakov lenient anyway in this siman only Shabbat also permitted — no marit ayin concern since all sell chametz on Pesach with land even on chol hamoed; since custom permitted in beer mixing, no marit ayin from all selling chametz — what difference Shabbat or weekday; therefore Shabbat better than other Shabbats of year — clear; I only wrote this to exclude minim who say opposite — wrote for remembrance, may mouth of falsehood be stopped; examine.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (1) After Pesach etc. He explained loaves; but when paying money, permitted even during Pesach.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [Levush] Forbidden etc. Bach permits b'dieved even without stipulation; if given flour or money it appears permitted to wear even chametz that had risen after Pesach; Chak Yaakov agreed; same law for one who buys allotment from Kutim who give fixed bread every week.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [Levush] He can etc. Specifically when he takes money from the start (Tur, Hagahot Maimoniyot, Bach, Magen Avraham); Taz strained Hagahot Maimoniyot's explanation that intent is l'chatchila permitted since he wants to take — per his version he takes money; not so for examiner in the text, rather he takes money and implies already took; and Taz for practical law l'chatchila permitted since he wants to take.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: (4) Before Pesach etc. However on Shabbat and four yom tov days forbidden as siman 245 (Magen Avraham); Chak Yaakov wondered and permits on yom tov since burning for need permitted — all the more no prohibition if Kutim act as his agent — so far; in my humble opinion Magen Avraham is reasonable: since such chametz unfit for a Jew, such burning is full prohibition even through a Kutim.
eliyah-rabbah/5:_: (5) Forbidden to receive etc. Even before Pesach.
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: (6) And if he received etc. Specifically before court became known they would forbid the wage; if court forbade and he received afterwards, forbidden to benefit (Bach); see end siman 443.
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: (7) Money permitted etc. But if he received loaves, forbidden to benefit, for he acquired them on Pesach since their custom is always to give loaves (Magen Avraham).
eshel-avraham/1:_: To repay him. For at repayment time the first is not in existence — not chametz substitutes; and likewise in Gemara regarding workers in Beit Rabbi Yannai — the poor borrow shevi'it produce in shevi'it and repay in eighth; all the more chametz that does not take its value.
eshel-avraham/7:א: In order to. See Be'er Heitev s.k. 13 what he wrote to permit in oven; Magen Avraham wrote it deals with his unstipulated wage and oven presumably for baking chametz — not so for utensil and donkey unstipulated permitted; with this resolve that Shulchan Aruch words do not contradict seif 4.
eshel-avraham/7:ב: Chametz. Tosafot Pesachim 22 implies: if a non-Jew's animal is laden with chametz, forbidden to unload except not in his presence. First version permitted because of animal's pain (Bach, end of his words).
eshel-avraham/7:ג: The custom. See siman 442 and 447 — we hold forbidden to sell to a non-Jew a chicken in which wheat was found even if he does not benefit from chametz; see Yoreh De'ah 54. Further therefore say a dish cooked in chametz utensil may be sold to a non-Jew; Ma'agalei Tzedek wrote it deals with utensils specifically for washing and bathing only (end of his words); see Taz in Yoreh De'ah there.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] A Jew who borrowed etc. — there are places that practiced not to borrow a loaf from a friend before Pesach to repay after Pesach; I suspect they touched it because of interest concern — lending se'ah bese'ah or loaf for loaf with fixed time forbidden (Riaz, Bach in Sefer HaGedolah chapter Kol Sha'ah; Darkei Moshe Orach Chayim 1; Kenesset HaGedolah in gloss; Magen Avraham s.k. 1). According to what our rabbi the author wrote Yoreh De'ah siman 462 seif 1 in gloss permitting loaf for loaf etc. (see there) it would appear to be lenient; however since Riaz himself did not decide they practiced for this reason but wrote "it appears" — do not be lenient where they practiced, possibly they practiced to forbid for another reason. Also where they did not practice prohibition, appears one should be stringent l'chatchila to borrow before Pesach and repay after Pesach, since Shulchan Aruch wording "a Jew borrowed" implies specifically if he borrowed and did not repay he must repay after Pesach; but l'chatchila he should repay before Pesach if possible.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There — he must repay etc. and there is no prohibition of chametz over which Passover passed since it was not in existence at prohibition time (Tur, Levush, Magen Avraham there; Kaf HaChayyim Orach Chayim 1). And he wrote there: if he repays money instead of loaf, even during Pesach permitted (see there). And so R' Yehuda Orach Chayim 1, R' Akiva Eiger Orach Chayim 1, R' Zalman Orach Chayim 1.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) There — he must repay etc. even if the first loaf was in existence, such as borrower erred or forgot to burn — must repay and give another loaf after Pesach (Ma'amar Mordechai Orach Chayim 1; and so Mekor Chayyim Orach Chayim 1, R' Akiva Eiger 1, Chayei Adam general rule 124 22).
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (4) There — he must repay etc. A Jew who lent chametz to a non-Jew before Pesach must repay chametz like it after Pesach, since he does not return the first chametz in existence — permitted (Riaz, Bach in Sefer HaGedolah chapter Kol Sha'ah; Kenesset HaGedolah in gloss). But Peri Chadash challenged and wrote even if he returns that chametz, permitted even for eating — since he lent to non-Jew it stood in his possession and is non-Jew's chametz over which Passover passed, permitted even for eating; and R' Akiva Eiger agreed there; R' Zalman Orach Chayim 2.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: (5) [Seif 2] He should tell him before Pesach etc. Taz s.k. 1 divides: if he can remove each week, stipulation before Pesach helps; but if he fixed interest once and cannot remove until set time between them, stipulation before Pesach does not help, must stipulate at transaction start, like siman 245 partnership matter (see there). However Noda BiYehudah Orach Chayim 1 wrote on Taz's words it is not compelled — even if cannot remove until set time, can stipulate before Pesach, unlike siman 245 (see there). And so Chamed Moshe Orach Chayim 2 and Meshivat Nefesh Orach Chayim 1, except Meshivat Nefesh wrote where dina demalkhuta neither can withdraw l'chatchila, be stringent like Taz, b'dieved requires further study (end) — but in Be'er Heitev wrote even there no stringency b'dieved (see there). And so Kaf HaChayyim Orach Chayim 3 wrote do not be stringent in these laws since Jew does not acquire without pulling per most poskim (see there).
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) There, and since he stipulated etc. — implies but if he did not stipulate, forbidden; as Beit Yosef in Avi HaEzri (see there). And so Levush. But Bach wrote l'chatchila concern Rabeinu Yerucham's view but b'dieved permitted even without any stipulation (see there). Bach, Magen Avraham s.k. 2; Chak Yosef Orach Chayim 2; Mekor Chayyim Orach Chayim 2; Chayei Adam general rule 124 14. Peri Chadash wrote no need to say anything beforehand — from default receives after Pesach chametz loaves that would have been given on Pesach, as Hagahot Maimoniyot and Mordechai Beit Yosef brought (see there). Kaf HaChayyim Orach Chayim 3 wrote main point as Shulchan Aruch and Levush — l'chatchila good to stipulate; if stipulates, even if non-Jew later gives chametz over which Passover passed, permitted; if not, if non-Jew gives flour, money, or post-Pesach chametz, permitted — chametz substitutes permitted as above siman 443; same for priests' allotment (meaning king gave priests their bread ration weekly, sold to Jew at year start for whole year's bread) giving fixed bread weekly; do not be stringent, Jew does not acquire without pulling per most poskim — Choshen Mishpat 194 and Shach s.k. 1 (end). However R' Zalman Orach Chayim 3 ruled like Bach — l'chatchila must stipulate; b'dieved if not, even if non-Jew brings after Pesach for Pesach week loaves that became chametz on Pesach, permitted to receive and eat. Orach Chayim 4 wrote same for priests' allotment — l'chatchila stipulate, b'dieved if not and after Pesach they give chametz bread for Pesach week, permitted to receive and eat (see there).
kaf-hachayyim/7:_: (7) And that R' Zalman wrote priests' bread permitted to eat — because it is like pat palter, made to distribute and give as gift, as Zevach Tzedek on Yoreh De'ah siman 112 24 in name of several poskim (see there). And what he wrote pat of interest permitted to eat — likewise if pat palter; but if pat of employer forbidden to eat, as Yoreh De'ah siman 112 seif 2; and that pat palter permitted specifically where practiced leniency with pat palter, as Yoreh De'ah there.
levushei-serad/1:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 3 — he tells the non-Jew etc. Beit Yosef in Hagahot Maimoniyot permits stipulating before Pesach and taking money etc.; and do not say to a Jew — so it should read.
levushei-serad/2:_: Taz s.k. 3 — the treasurer brought after Pesach and forbidden; say here too — so it should read.
levushei-serad/3:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 4 — as siman 443 etc.; and for Bach here too forbidden since he himself rented it; and so Bach this siman 90 s.k. 7 Peri Chadash.
levushei-serad/4:_: Taz s.k. 6 — how is permission to take on Shabbat what the mill grinds on Shabbat — a measure for it; Shabbat wage clearly forbidden etc. — so it should read.
levushei-serad/5:_: (Gloss) And some permit heating etc. See Mishna Berurah general rule 80 s.k. 15 Taz.
levushei-serad/6:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 12 — or command the grinders etc. — refers when he does not rent the mill itself, then no prohibition only because when he places in mill he acquires — therefore this remedy helps, unlike when renting mill itself, all the more if Jew must repair them — this remedy does not help, like oven — requires further study.
peri-megadim/1:_: He should say. Taz brought what Beit Yosef wrote — one who bought priests' allotment appears no need to say at all, nevertheless Shulchan Aruch ruled stringent l'chatchila and b'dieved permitted without statement; Magen Avraham 2. But Taz holds for practical law: wherever he lent a sum to a non-Jew and stipulated for a term up to a year etc. that the non-Jew cannot remove principal during the term — then the Jew acquired at loan start all year's loaves, must say initially that for Pesach week he gives money not loaves — stipulation before Pesach does not help; like siman 245 seif 1 requires giving initially; priests' allotment likewise since cannot remove all year, must give initially. Not so if each week the non-Jew can remove principal to lender — each week's stipulation at week start is like initial stipulation, permitted; and so in Magen Avraham it will be explained there is division between that Shabbat case and here; also the Jew did not acquire all year's loaves at loan start — Jew from non-Jew requires pulling, and even Jew from Jew — since d'rabbanan requires pulling, one might say no bal yera'eh transgression; further it is ownerless. However where dina demalkhuta neither can withdraw l'chatchila, be stringent like Taz; b'dieved requires further study. What Taz wrote on partnership oven seif 3 permitted Jew stipulate before Pesach to give money first before Pesach week for Pesach week as Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 1 Choshen Mishpat sign 3 Beit Yosef brought — wording strained: since Jew can divide partnership anytime, it would be like priests' allotment and interest removable each week — obviously permitted; I again saw his words clear: he holds whoever stipulated at partnership start for a term neither can withdraw — in oven certainly even if says before Pesach he wants only money not loaves, does not help, already acquired Pesach week's bread by dina demalkhuta — condition does not help as siman 245, unless can divide partnership anytime — therefore condition before Pesach for Pesach week money after Pesach permitted, like stipulation from partnership start; but stipulating before Pesach "take yours for Pesach and I afterwards" is not a condition before Pesach — chametz substitutes, for he tells non-Jew take my share in Pesach week etc.; therefore wondered on Mechaber seif 3 permitting take your bread-share in Pesach week etc.; what is written in sign 2 — Jew already has share each week — do not say can divide each week; rather: even before Pesach no condition here, telling non-Jew take my share on Pesach etc. — they are partners on Pesach and Jew afterwards takes chametz substitutes he acquired — as said; and so sign 2 will explain further.
peri-megadim/2:_: He tells him. Taz — and the content of his intent I explained in sign 1: even though Jew can withdraw from partnership each week, nevertheless not like initial stipulation (like interest if can remove principal each week — permitted), for no uprooting of partnership — only says for his Pesach share he will take afterwards — that is forbidden. What is written Tur in Rashi's name: what is written to take money means after Pesach; if he takes money, permitted since stipulated before Pesach he does not want partnership on Pesach unless he takes money — permitted after Pesach to take money; likewise chametz — money substitutes, as Avi HaEzri on interest likewise here since can remove partnership anytime, like initial condition; these show our master Taz had special intent in Tur (end of his words) responsum of Rashi: Jew should say before Pesach and take money from that week for future after Pesach — stipulate before Pesach to take afterwards money, then even chametz on erev Pesach in non-Jew's possession, money substitutes, permitted. Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 1 chametz sign 3 brought permitted to stipulate before Pesach and take money of that week; do not say Jew and non-Jew with field partnership etc.; but here since he takes money first, permitted, so Beit Yosef and Hagahot Maimoniyot in some versions I saw: but here when he takes money first, permitted — this is Taz's version: explanation "and takes money" after Pesach, from the start permitted to receive money — we do not forbid profiting from issurei hana'ah l'chatchila elsewhere except yayin nesech (there even b'dieved forbidden); need not take money before Pesach at all; likewise chametz can receive afterwards, money substitutes. Therefore no contradiction from Rashi's wording Tur brings implying no need to take money before Pesach, from Hagahot Maimoniyot and as said. In Magen Avraham sign 3 wrote Taz variant "takes" — lacking (typo in print there); intent Taz reads "and takes" with vav; but version "and took" without vav as Beit Yosef; in Hagahot Maimoniyot some prints I found with vav "and takes" as written. Further Taz wrote what Beit Yosef wrote Mordechai did not mention taking money before Pesach — on this Taz wrote Hagahot Maimoniyot also did not require taking money before Pesach, else why not write initially stipulate before Pesach and take money that week before Pesach; from not mentioning at start, implies no need before Pesach; and Tur in Rashi responsum wrote stipulate before Pesach and take money from that week, did not conclude take money before Pesach. (Tosafot typo should read "and further") further chametz permitted after Pesach, money substitutes — all who stipulate before Pesach to take afterwards money; and Taz wrote l'chatchila permitted afterwards to receive, we do not forbid profiting from issurei hana'ah except yayin nesech (there even b'dieved forbidden); and see sign 3 further; Magen Avraham sign 8 from this.
peri-megadim/3:א: Even. Taz — see signs 1 and 2: Tur brought Rashi responsum take money etc. — what Mechaber brought seif 3, omitted take money, relied on what Mordechai wrote first chapter Avodah Zarah siman 448 — Maharam asked regarding Jew and non-Jew with partnership oven etc., answered stipulation before Pesach permitted; see sign 2 what Taz challenged and what one may say. Afterwards Tur and R' Shimshon b. Avraham forbade in practice etc. — what Mechaber brought seif 4, as Be'er HaGolah noted; and since Tur and Rashba with vav imply disputing Rashi responsum — but unrelated: Rashi had condition before Pesach, Rashba Jew's oven etc.; also loaves they baked on Pesach — obviously Rashi agrees forbidden; money are chametz substitutes (what is l'chatchila is for Rashba who ruled b'dieved permitted, Eshel Avraham sign 5). Therefore dispute of Rashi and Rashba: Rashba forbids non-Jew's chametz in benefit during Pesach — profiting from issurei hana'ah (therefore what Rashba forbids taking money even before Pesach — see Magen Avraham sign 4). Rashi holds non-Jew's chametz during Pesach permitted in benefit — therefore no profiting from issurei hana'ah here etc. If so, at first glance Shulchan Aruch rulings contradict: seif 4 like seif 3 even partnership oven even if non-Jew can remove anytime and say he does not want to partner Pesach week and oven stands empty or they bake other things — nevertheless like partnership start as sign 1 end, still profiting from issurei hana'ah, wage of issurei hana'ah forbidden l'chatchila elsewhere; no remedy for seif 3 except at oven purchase start they stipulate Pesach week oven belongs to non-Jew, week after to Jew — then permitted not against will, as explained. Nevertheless difficult what Rashi holds non-Jew's chametz permitted in benefit during Pesach — difficult, Gemara Pesachim 29a concludes R' Avraham retracted; better explain Rashi permits profiting from other issurei hana'ah as above. For practical law: three seifim do not contradict — partnership oven is different; whoever stipulates before Pesach is as if stipulated at partnership start — proper. With this understand Kenesset HaGedolah glosses Beit Yosef sign 4 (see there) and siman 245 — condition before Shabbat only helps at partnership start, there appears as his agent, as Magen Avraham sign 3 and Taz per his view signs 1-2; not so seif 4 Jew's oven — condition does not help even before Pesach, forbidden to take money, ultimately profiting from issurei hana'ah; and hirer of donkey seif 7 — as Magen Avraham sign 11. All when partnership oven; but if rented oven from non-Jew to bake and both can remove anytime, even Taz agrees stipulation before Pesach helps non-Jew bake Pesach week, no profiting from issurei hana'ah, as Kenesset HaGedolah said.
peri-megadim/3:ב: And what challenged on Rashba — prohibition not pleased to acquire — not body of law forbidding profiting from issurei hana'ah; rather loaves forbidden because he acquired oven like his field and Jew's chametz over which Passover passed forbidden by law; prohibition not pleased to acquire — answered he is pleased since he left to bake etc. (end of his words); see Magen Avraham; and see there further.
peri-megadim/4:_: There is. Taz — regarding profiting from other issurei hana'ah some are lenient even l'chatchila like hiring donkey per one explanation; also siman 256 seif 3 (typo 215) — there Torah prohibition and not trusted, unlike here even d'rabbanan prohibition unclear. However if d'rabbanan prohibition clear, do not create initial safek d'rabbanan (Magen Avraham 467 2).
peri-megadim/5:_: House. Taz and Magen Avraham sign 16 and Beit Yosef in Agur — specifically during Pesach or erev Pesach, unreasonable to forbid thirty days before Pesach; meaning certainly Yerushalmi means erev Pesach, cannot say they forbade unstipulated generally — obviously at least thirty days before permitted, not dealing with unstipulated; likewise one may say specifically erev Pesach but Darkei Moshe brought within thirty forbidden, before thirty permitted (end of his words); requires further study.
peri-megadim/6:א: Forbidden. Taz — per his view sign 4 regarding profiting from issurei hana'ah forbidden, likewise seif 3.
peri-megadim/6:ב: What is written on estates. Magen Avraham — two difficulties: one, a person does not sell something not yet in existence, not a sale at all — see priests' allotment what to examine. Two, if non-Jew bought he only bought when it came to existence, and we all the more permit eating from seller — not like this. One may say: even though a person does not transfer something not in existence, he can remove himself from it like hefker — can declare hefker even for not in existence, as Bach responsum 124 hefker from vow reason, person forbids himself not in existence — see R' David seif 64, Magen Avraham 1; likewise here Jew can remove from them before Pesach siman 441 Taz end what is written there. What is written one with his own mills — no remedy except sell to non-Jew with absorption — I do not know — he may sell mill itself any erev Pesach and it appears should read "and rent with absorption" — but complete sale of mill body appears permitted any erev Pesach and as said.
peri-megadim/7:_: And to wash in them — not from absorption; Taz and Bach wrote wanting continued existence — he benefits from chametz not further absorbed since already absorbed — should have been forbidden; but we do not hold so; wanting continued existence has dispute — Magen Avraham 11; if so explained there; see Taz sign 4 what is written there.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 4 — he acquired them on Pesach. In my humble opinion: even though he acquired on Pesach, nevertheless his loaf-share was not clarified which he acquired — became partner with non-Jew — say no clarification, perhaps he received the non-Jew's share; see Sha'agat Aryeh and Chak Yaakov siman 440.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Seif 6 — And forbidden to buy chametz for non-Jew on Pesach. Told non-Jew on Pesach to buy chametz and he bought for him — one may say: even for poskim who hold agency for non-Jew stringently (see Yoreh De'ah siman 169) — nevertheless only d'rabbanan and permitted after Pesach; and on Pesach if b'dieved — one may say need not burn it; and regarding acquisition through apostate — debate if we say regarding apostate "inclined to idolatry" and Jew did not buy and apostate did not buy since he did not want to acquire — word of gematria to Gaon Porat Yosef parashat Korach; see his book Eshel Avraham above siman 305.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 12 — with this Tur does not dispute; I find it hard to know Tur who forbids renting — vessel itself does not absorb and even if he does not take money for absorption — if so even leaving dry forbidden.
yad-ephraim/1:_: See in Magen Avraham — and even though if he hired him for other work and afterwards did yayin nesech with him his wage forbidden — there, if he did nothing he would not pay, and he takes yayin nesech wage; but here, since he rented oven for a week, even if non-Jew baked nothing he would pay — he does not take chametz wage, therefore permitted. What we learn permits when he does the other work and payment is not for those barrels — see Beit Yosef.
